video_title: Will Yaxel Lendeborg CARRY Warriors with Steph Curry INJURED?!

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Warriors' struggle to finish games without a marquee scorer
quotes.excerpt: They don't have that one marquee guy to finish games.

text_blocks.speaker: Lou Williams
text_blocks.text: Last night was a sample size. Those guys competed. They did everything they could to continue to get themselves in the game. They just didn't have enough to finish. They don't have that one marquee guy to finish games. Yaxel Lendeborg is playing lights out as a rookie. Super impressed with what he's doing and the way that he carries himself, the way that he plays, his pace. Sometimes he brings the ball up, he can create off the dribble, you can throw it to him in the post, he's going to take advantage of his size. He's a three-level scorer at this point in his young career, but he hasn't markeed himself to be the guy that can finish games for them in that Steph Curry.

text_blocks.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
text_blocks.text: Without a doubt. This was kind of the writing on the wall, especially with how he's been playing. You have your oldest guy on the team, he's putting up historic numbers this late in his career. Obviously, if he was to go down, it's going to plummet the rest of the team. You just can't go find 30 to 35 points on the bench on a random night. It's going to be tough for the Warriors. This is part of the issue I have with how they built this team around him.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Warriors' offensive challenges and rotations without Steph Curry
quotes.excerpt: They are going to have to face different coverages now without him on the floor.
quotes.quote: The way that you approach the Warriors and defend the Warriors has a lot to do with Steph Curry and the double teams and the spacing and the attention that he gets opens up the floor for the Yaxel Lendeborgs and the Draymond Greens and the Meltons. They are going to have to face different coverages now without him on the floor with all that attention towards him. We've already seen Steve Kerr lines up his rotations when Steph Curry is out, Yaxel Lendeborg is in. When Yaxel Lendeborg is out, Steph Curry is in. They can't do that now, which is going to be tough with Steph Curry. Hopefully he's not out for too much time.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Yaxel Lendeborg's impressive rookie performance and scoring ability
quotes.excerpt: He's averaging 21, 7 and 4. No matter what his age is, he's still really good.
quotes.quote: Yaxel Lendeborg has proven in a short time here, 12 games, this kid's been unbelievable. I see a lot of stuff, he's 24 years old. Look at his numbers. I don't care if he's 30 years old. He's averaging 21, 7 and 4. No matter what his age is, he's still really good at basketball and having a hell of a year. I don't care that he's an older rookie. He has exceeded expectations so much and he's tough, he's fearless. He's picking battles with Luka Doncic. He's isoing Kevin Durant last night. You can just tell he's embracing these matchups.

quotes.speaker: Michelle Beadle
quotes.summary_phrase: Darius Acuff's historic start as a rookie point guard
quotes.excerpt: He set the record for the most points by any rookie point guard in NBA history.
quotes.quote: Darius Acuff set the record for the most points by any rookie point guard in NBA history through 10 games. Do the Kings have their new franchise player?

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: Darius Acuff's potential as a future franchise player
quotes.excerpt: He's a star in the making. I mean, he's here.
quotes.quote: Yes, they do have their franchise player. He's a star in the making. I mean, he's here. It's just about him learning how to obviously lead a professional group, gain experience in this game, and just keep growing as a player in the league. I think he's got to go through the steps that everybody else has had to go through. He's showing that he has a promising future. He's leading by example, he's a hard worker, he's a good kid, everything you're looking for in a franchise guy.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Darius Acuff's efficiency and potential with a better roster
quotes.excerpt: His efficiency will continue to get better when they surround him with a better roster.
quotes.quote: There's no doubt the kid's a bucket. I think his efficiency will continue to get better when they surround him with a better roster and more talent. He doesn't have to take half of these low-percent, highly contested shots. This is in his blood. He's been doing this since high school, he did it in college. He is just an absolute walking bucket. So no matter who they add around him, he's still going to have that firepower to go and score 20, 30 points on any given night.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Comparing Darius Acuff to Allen Iverson and individual development
quotes.excerpt: Let's allow Darius Acuff to become the best version of himself.
quotes.quote: I like the comparison, but listen, we've made it cool, we've heard it since the draft, now let's get over it. Let's allow Darius Acuff to become the best version of himself and carve out a lane for himself and do historical things in his own right. Because soon as something doesn't go right, we're going to go back to the Allen Iverson comparison. Soon as something does go right, we're going to go back to the Allen Iverson comparison. Just allow these young guys to create waves for themselves and to be their own guys.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Darius Acuff's ceiling and the need for team success
quotes.excerpt: We're going to always want to see him do it when it matters the most.
quotes.quote: It all depends on their team success. Ceiling wise, it's what he's averaging now and be a perennial scorer in this league. It's just we're going to always want to see him do it when it matters the most, in the postseason and on a competing basketball team. This team feels like they're ways away from being even solid and sniffing the play-in, let alone being on a contending team. That's nothing to do with him. Obviously, being on a lesser team like this has given him a lot more opportunity and keys and freedom than he would have if he got drafted to a powerhouse team.
